title: Four Boys, One Tap: The Real Homework PDF on the Kiosk TV | vitalii.no
description:
My four kids' weekly school plans only ever existed as PDF attachments buried in email threads. The kitchen kiosk calendar already showed homework notes, but if a child wanted to see the actual ukeplan page — the real layout the teacher sent — there was no way to find it from the TV at all.

A background script now watches the family's email archive for any attachment named like a weekly plan and stores it twice: the PDF's own text untouched in a database table, and every page rendered to a wide image in a second table. A new full-screen screen on the kiosk fetches those pages through a Cloudflare Worker and stacks them at full width, with arrow buttons jumping to the nearest week that actually has a stored plan. The ingest only processes each attachment once, so nothing duplicates.

Each of the four boys can now open his own week's real ukeplan straight from the kiosk calendar and scroll through it page by page, instead of a parent having to dig the PDF out of email and show it on a phone.
